source:
Reports request-matcher registrations (requestMatchers, mvcMatchers, antMatchers, regexMatchers) that are chained after anyRequest() inside an authorizeHttpRequests / authorizeRequests block.

anyRequest() must be the last matcher in the authorization chain. Configuring another matcher after it makes Spring Security fail at startup with Can't configure requestMatchers after anyRequest.

Incorrect:


  http.authorizeHttpRequests(auth -> auth
    .requestMatchers("/", "/home").permitAll()
    .anyRequest().authenticated()
    .requestMatchers("/admin/**").hasRole("ADMIN")   // reports: configured after anyRequest()
  );

Correct (move anyRequest() to the end):


  http.authorizeHttpRequests(auth -> auth
    .requestMatchers("/", "/home").permitAll()
    .requestMatchers("/admin/**").hasRole("ADMIN")
    .anyRequest().authenticated()
  );
target:
Meldet Registrierungen von Request-Matchern (requestMatchers, mvcMatchers, antMatchers, regexMatchers), die nach anyRequest() innerhalb eines authorizeHttpRequests- / authorizeRequests-Blocks verkettet werden.

anyRequest() muss der letzte Matcher in der Autorisierungskette sein. Wird danach ein weiterer Matcher konfiguriert, schlägt Spring Security beim Start mit Can't configure requestMatchers after anyRequest fehl.

Falsch:


  http.authorizeHttpRequests(auth -> auth
    .requestMatchers("/", "/home").permitAll()
    .anyRequest().authenticated()
    .requestMatchers("/admin/**").hasRole("ADMIN")   // gemeldet: nach anyRequest() konfiguriert
  );

Richtig (anyRequest() ans Ende verschieben):


  http.authorizeHttpRequests(auth -> auth
    .requestMatchers("/", "/home").permitAll()
    .requestMatchers("/admin/**").hasRole("ADMIN")
    .anyRequest().authenticated()
  );
